Thanksgiving 2023: the first Neuron RFC lands in vLLM.

title: Private Inference — confidential computing, with strict controls over prompts and responses while they're being processed by a model, is now in testing:
title_en: Private Inference — confidential computing, with strict controls over prompts and responses while they're being processed by a model, is now in testing:
title_zh: 机密计算私有推理技术进入测试阶段
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI is testing 'Private Inference' utilizing confidential computing to ensure prompts and responses remain encrypted during model processing. By leveraging Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), the architecture aims to eliminate third-party or cloud provider access to sensitive inference data, strengthening enterprise-grade AI security.
summary_zh: OpenAI 正在测试名为“私有推理”的机密计算技术，旨在模型处理提示词与响应期间实现高等级的数据合规与隐私防护。
full_text_zh: 私人推理 - 机密计算，在模型处理提示和响应时对其进行严格控制，目前正在测试中：
full_text_en: Private Inference — confidential computing, with strict controls over prompts and responses while they're being processed by a model, is now in testing:

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI 正在推进基于机密计算（Confidential Computing）的私有推理架构，旨在确保用户提示词（Prompt）与模型生成内容在处理全生命周期内处于隔离加密状态。此举核心在于利用可信执行环境（TEE）屏蔽包括云服务商在内的第三方访问权限，提升企业级 AI 应用在处理敏感数据时的安全性。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI is testing 'Private Inference' utilizing confidential computing to ensure prompts and responses remain encrypted during model processing. By leveraging Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), the architecture aims to eliminate third-party or cloud provider access to sensitive inference data, strengthening enterprise-grade AI security.

elements_zh.where: AI 推理计算基础设施
elements_zh.what: 测试私有推理（Private Inference）技术，通过机密计算实现全链路处理隐私控制
elements_zh.why: 满足金融、医疗及政府机构对大规模语言模型推理过程的数据主权与隐私保护合规要求

elements_en.what: Testing Private Inference via confidential computing for strict prompt/response privacy control
elements_en.why: Meeting strict data sovereignty and privacy compliance requirements for enterprise-level AI applications

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 私有推理技术的落地将重构大模型商业竞争范式，从单纯的算力堆叠转向计算机密性与合规能力的博弈。通过将隐私边界下沉至硬件级可信执行环境，AI 提供商能够有效解决企业部署 AI 时的最大合规掣肘，从而进一步加速敏感数据场景下大模型的行业化渗透。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The deployment of private inference shifts AI competition from pure compute scaling to the management of data confidentiality and regulatory compliance. By anchoring privacy boundaries in hardware-level TEEs, AI providers can eliminate critical barriers for sensitive-data environments, accelerating enterprise adoption across regulated sectors.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: OpenAI 正在推进基于机密计算（Confidential Computing）的私有推理架构，旨在确保用户提示词（Prompt）与模型生成内容在处理全生命周期内处于隔离加密状态。此举核心在于利用可信执行环境（TEE）屏蔽包括云服务商在内的第三方访问权限，提升企业级 AI 应用在处理敏感数据时的安全性。
ai_analysis.digest_en: OpenAI is testing 'Private Inference' utilizing confidential computing to ensure prompts and responses remain encrypted during model processing. By leveraging Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), the architecture aims to eliminate third-party or cloud provider access to sensitive inference data, strengthening enterprise-grade AI security.
key_points_zh: 企业级客户对大模型处理隐私数据的合规性焦虑驱动技术研发
利用可信执行环境（TEE）在推理阶段实现数据全链路加解密保护
该技术将成为大模型厂商获取B端核心市场的重要信任基石
key_points_en: Driven by enterprise concerns over data privacy in LLM processing
Implementation of TEE for end-to-end encryption during inference
Critical trust infrastructure for capturing high-value B2B market share
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 私有推理技术的落地将重构大模型商业竞争范式，从单纯的算力堆叠转向计算机密性与合规能力的博弈。通过将隐私边界下沉至硬件级可信执行环境，AI 提供商能够有效解决企业部署 AI 时的最大合规掣肘，从而进一步加速敏感数据场景下大模型的行业化渗透。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: The deployment of private inference shifts AI competition from pure compute scaling to the management of data confidentiality and regulatory compliance. By anchoring privacy boundaries in hardware-level TEEs, AI providers can eliminate critical barriers for sensitive-data environments, accelerating enterprise adoption across regulated sectors.

title_en:
What happens when AI starts helping build better AI?

That's the idea behind Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI): a system improves, keeps the gain, and uses it to improve again. Researchers now map it across 6 levels, from one-off fixes to systems that improve the improvement process itself.

Early systems already automate parts of the loop. One coding agent went from 20% to 50% on its benchmark subset. But the top level hasn't been shown yet, and humans still set the goals.

title: Uber 为 5,000 个工具构建了 MCP 网关。感人的。它仅适用于 Uber 自己的代理商。我下了相反的赌注。 TADA 和 Throo 对任何代理商、任何建筑商开放，无需许可会议。呼叫真正的司机，全额付款，0% 佣金。开放就是开放的意思。
title_en: Uber built an MCP gateway for 5,000 tools. Impressive. It is for Uber's own agents only. I took the opposite bet. TADA and Throo are open to any agent, any builder, no permission meeting. Call a real driver, pay in full, 0% commission. Open means open.
title_zh: Uber发布MCP网关与开放生态之争
full_text_zh: Uber 为 5,000 个工具构建了 MCP 网关。感人的。它仅适用于 Uber 自己的代理商。我下了相反的赌注。 TADA 和 Throo 对任何代理商、任何建筑商开放，无需许可会议。呼叫真正的司机，全额付款，0% 佣金。开放就是开放的意思。
full_text_en: Uber built an MCP gateway for 5,000 tools. Impressive. It is for Uber's own agents only. I took the opposite bet. TADA and Throo are open to any agent, any builder, no permission meeting. Call a real driver, pay in full, 0% commission. Open means open.
summary_zh: Uber为内部AI代理构建MCP网关以统一交互标准，引发初创开发者关于闭环生态与许可制商业模式的公开挑战。
summary_en: Uber has deployed a Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway for its internal AI agents to standardize interaction interfaces. Developers are challenging this closed-loop strategy, advocating for permissionless, commission-free architectures like TADA and Throo as alternatives for open ecosystem participation.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Uber近期为其内部AI代理部署了模型上下文协议（MCP）网关以标准化交互接口。开发者社区成员针对其闭环运营模式提出异议，并倡导通过TADA与Throo等无需许可的分布式协议实现无佣金的直接交易机制。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Uber has deployed a Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway for its internal AI agents to standardize interaction interfaces. Developers are challenging this closed-loop strategy, advocating for permissionless, commission-free architectures like TADA and Throo as alternatives for open ecosystem participation.

elements_zh.where: AI代理开发与协议架构领域
elements_zh.what: Uber部署MCP网关以强化内部系统互通，遭初创开发者抵制并提出去中心化替代方案
elements_zh.why: 围绕AI代理数据交互标准的归属权及平台佣金模式的市场主导权争夺

elements_en.who: Uber; Independent developers (TADA and Throo projects)
elements_en.where: AI agent development and protocol architecture
elements_en.what: Uber implemented an MCP gateway for internal systems, triggering pushback from developers favoring permissionless, zero-commission protocols.
elements_en.why: Contention over control of AI agent interoperability standards and platform monetization models.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI代理的标准化战争正在从模型层转向接口层，MCP（模型上下文协议）本质是各巨头争夺生态控制权的入场券。Uber意在构建受控的垂直生态以抽成，而去中心化协议试图通过绕过中介来打破大模型的平台垄断，这将成为未来AI服务分发模式的核心分歧点。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The war for AI agent standardization is shifting from model training to interface protocols, where MCP acts as a strategic gatekeeper for ecosystem control. Uber’s move aims to enforce a vertical, rent-extracting ecosystem, while permissionless alternatives prioritize bypassing intermediaries to disrupt platform hegemony, defining the next fracture in AI service delivery.

开发者群体质疑其封闭性并推崇去中心化架构
零佣金模式与平台许可制的商业模式直接冲突
key_points_en: Uber integrates internal agent architecture using MCP protocols.
Developers challenge the move as overly restrictive.
Direct conflict between zero-commission protocols and platform-gatekeeper business models.

Uber’s move aims to enforce a vertical, rent-extracting ecosystem, while permissionless alternatives prioritize bypassing intermediaries to disrupt platform hegemony, defining the next fracture in AI service delivery.

We made a billing mistake at launch of GPT-6.2 that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users. 

We’ve fixed this now, so the same work will use more of your plan’s usage allowance. Comparing to last week, you will reach your limits 40% faster on GPT-6.2 Astra and 25% faster on Sol. title: I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :) - 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USG
title_en:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://karpathy.ai/usaciv/ and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:
title_zh:
我要求克劳德用来自美国的真实数据填充文明风格的游戏地图。 Opus 5.5 下载并解析了大量公共数据以及 7 小时和 45K 行代码……它可以工作了:)

- 31 个真实数据源，包括人口普查、BEA、BLS、EIA、NOAA、USGS、D
author: Andrej Karpathy
author_role: Eureka Labs 创始人 / 前特斯拉 AI 总监与 OpenAI 科学家
summary_zh:
oD、NPS、FAA、FEMA、CDC...
- 实际海拔、土地覆盖、GDP、就业、发电厂、矿山、港口、机场、基地、公园、大学、货运、灾害；所有这些都被协调到一个 25 公里的六角网格上。
- 数据被转换成文明语言，例如黄金收益率就是GDP。一个城市的地区是其真正的行业专业化：圣何塞有一个园区，底特律是“汽车城”。它的公民是真正的劳动力：圣何塞四分之一的工人是工程师、编码员或科学家，而全国只有四分之一。奇观是根据公布的规则来选择的，例如国家公园是根据游客数量来选择的，大学是根据研发支出来选择的，等等。
- 19 个镜头（收入、学位、信仰、灾难……）、524 条地铁的城市景观，以及 9 名顾问和 1 名探险家。 Explorer 将 3,100 多个县中任何一个县的任何列转换为链接到地图的表格和散点图。
- 克劳德决定跳过一些州和领地
- 使用 Claude Code 桌面应用程序、Opus 5.5 在介质上构建并打开超级代码。

它部署在这里：https://karpathy.ai/usaciv/ 和“？”也有源码链接。我不太清楚我要做什么，但浏览和玩起来真的很有趣。也许它可以扩展或内置到游戏中。我每周的克劳德引言只剩下一半了，所以其他人必须接替:D。克劳德还制作了预告片：

title_en:
🆕 New 12B model! One of my favorite SMALL local coding models just got a new sibling!  

🟢 RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, RTX 5070 12GB, RTX 5080 16GB — this one's for you!

Mellum2.1 Instruct.

And it uses HALF the output tokens of its Thinking counterpart while achieving 86% of its SWE-bench Verified score.

I've covered JetBrains Mellum several times, and it performed surprisingly well in my own testing 

BUT you can't turn off thinking no matter how hard  you try.

Back in October, I covered Mellum2.1 Thinking and its new MTP head, which JetBrains said could accelerate decoding by up to 1.8×.

Now JetBrains is back with a NEW model.

It's a non-thinking coding model designed for fast local agents, tool calling, repository work, and sub-agents.

JetBrains' reported SWE-bench Verified scores ...
⚪ Mellum2 Instruct → 20.2%
🔥 Mellum2.1 Instruct → 40.4% 👈
🧠 Mellum2.1 Thinking → 47.0%

That's 2x the previous Instruct model's score.
But here's the really interesting part.

🎯 The new Instruct model achieves 86% of its Thinking sibling's SWE-bench Verified score.

While generating roughly HALF as many tokens on JetBrains' repository-level validation tasks.

No explicit thinking traces.

Fewer tokens. Less compute spent generating answers. Potentially faster local agent workflows.

And the model is still SMALL.

🧠 12B total / 2.5B active
📚 131K context
🔓 Apache 2.0
💻 Official GGUFs
🦙 llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio
🤖 Coding, tool calling, repository agents

Official quants ...

🟢 MXFP4_MOE → 7.0GB
🟢 Q4_K_M → 8.1GB
🟢 Q6_K → 10.9GB
🟢 Q8_0 → 12.9GB

And yes, JetBrains released a new MTP head specifically for Instruct.

The combined Q4_K_M + MTP build is just 8.4GB.
JetBrains also reports improvements over Mellum2 

Instruct in:
🔥 AIME → 32.3 to 61.1
🔥 WorkBench → 22.2 to 38.0
🔥 SWE-bench Verified → 20.2 to 40.4
The secret is in the post-training.

JetBrains used reinforcement learning in real software repositories, allowing the model to interact with files, execute shell commands, and learn from passing or failing tests.

They also tuned the training to encourage shorter, direct answers.

I've been a fan of Mellum for a while, and this new Instruct version looks like a great candidate for local coding agents.

author: @TeksEdge
summary_zh:
是 Thinking 对应产品的一半，同时达到了 SWE 基准验证分数的 86%。

我已经多次介绍过 JetBrains Mellum，它在我自己的测试中表现出奇的好

但无论你多么努力，你都无法停止思考。

早在 10 月份，我就介绍了 Mellum2.1 Thinking 及其新的 MTP 头，JetBrains 表示该头可以将解码速度提高高达 1.8 倍。

现在 JetBrains 带着新模型回来了。

它是一种非思考编码模型，专为快速本地代理、工具调用、存储库工作和子代理而设计。

JetBrains 报告的 SWE 基准验证分数...
⚪ Mellum2 指导 → 20.2%
🔥 Mellum2.1 指导 → 40.4% 👈
🧠 Mellum2.1 思维 → 47.0%

这是之前 Instruct 模型分数的 2 倍。
但这是真正有趣的部分。

🎯新的指令模型达到了86%的思维兄弟的SWE-bench验证分数。

在 JetBrains 的存储库级验证任务上生成大约一半的令牌。

没有明确的思维痕迹。

更少的代币。生成答案所需的计算量更少。可能更快的本地代理工作流程。

而且型号还是小。

🧠 总计 12B / 活跃 2.5B
📚 131K 上下文
🔓 阿帕奇 2.0
💻 官方 GGUF
🦙 llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio
🤖 编码、工具调用、存储库代理

官方量化...

🟢 MXFP4_MOE → 7.0GB
🟢 Q4_K_M → 8.1GB
🟢 Q6_K → 10.9GB
🟢 Q8_0 → 12.9GB

是的，JetBrains 专门为 Instruct 发布了一款新的 MTP 头。

Q4_K_M + MTP 的组合版本仅为 8.4GB。
JetBrains 还报告了相对 Mellum2 的改进

指导：
🔥 AIME → 32.3 至 61.1
🔥 工作台 → 22.2 至 38.0
🔥 SWE 工作台验证 → 20.2 至 40.4
秘密就在后期训练中。

JetBrains 在真实的软件存储库中使用强化学习，允许模型与文件交互、执行 shell 命令以及从通过或失败的测试中学习。

他们还调整了培训以鼓励更简短、直接的答案。

我已经是 Mellum 的粉丝有一段时间了，这个新的 Instruct 版本看起来非常适合本地编码代理。

title_en:
In Text to Video, MAGI-2 brings strong physics and visual craft, but audio and dialogue hold it to #7

From a text prompt alone on AA-Video-T2V v2.1, MAGI-2 climbs 14 places over MAGI-2 Preview and ranks #2 in Physics, #3 in Human Anatomy and Complex Composition, and #4 in Lighting & Materials and Live-Action Film.

Even with visual quality ahead of Dreamina Seedance 2.5 in Physics and Lighting & Materials, spoken dialogue (Dialogue & Lip Sync), audio timing (Audio Synchronization), and explainer videos (Productivity & Knowledge Work) remain furthest behind the leaders.

➤ Physics covers mechanics, thermal effects, material interactions, fracture and deformation, optics, cause and effect, and counterfactual physics.

➤ Lighting & Materials covers lighting, exposure, shadows, color temperature, texture, cloth, hair and fur.

➤ Dialogue & Lip Sync covers single- and multi-speaker dialogue, and voiceover vs on-screen speech.

➤ Audio Synchronization covers diegetic sound effects, background music and score, and on- and off-screen sound.

➤ Productivity & Knowledge Work covers explainers, educational and training videos, animated data visualizations, and scenario simulations.

full_text_zh:
在文本到视频中，MAGI-2 带来了强大的物理和视觉工艺，但音频和对话使其保持在#7

仅从 AA-Video-T2V v2.1 上的文本提示来看，MAGI-2 就比 MAGI-2 Preview 上升了 14 位，在物理领域排名第 2，在人体解剖学和复杂构图领域排名第 3，在灯光与材质和真人电影领域排名第 4。

即使视觉质量在物理、灯光和材料方面领先于 Dreamina Seedance 2.5，口语对话（对话和唇形同步）、音频定时（音频同步）和解说视频（生产力和知识工作）仍然远远落后于领先者。

➤ 物理学涵盖力学、热效应、材料相互作用、断裂和变形、光学、因果关系以及反事实物理学。

➤ 灯光和材质涵盖灯光、曝光、阴影、色温、纹理、布料、头发和毛皮。

➤ 对话和口型同步涵盖单人和多扬声器对话，以及画外音与屏幕语音。

➤ 音频同步涵盖剧情音效、背景音乐和乐谱、屏幕内外声音。

➤ 生产力和知识工作涵盖解释、教育和培训视频、动画数据可视化和场景模拟。

title: This tool shows which LLMs you can run locally on your PC 🔥 and it just hit 32K+ GitHub stars: It’s called llmfit. Before you download a model, it checks your CPU, GPU, RAM and VRAM. Then it ranks models for your setup across four dimensions. > Fit: will the
title_en:
This tool shows which LLMs you can run locally on your PC 🔥 and it just hit 32K+ GitHub stars:

It’s called llmfit. Before you download a model, it checks your CPU, GPU, RAM and VRAM. Then it ranks models for your setup across four dimensions.

> Fit: will the model fit in memory?  
> Speed: how many tokens per second can you expect?  
> Quality: how do model size and quantization affect the estimate?  
> Context: how much text can the model handle at once?

If a model is too big, llmfit works down through smaller quantized versions until it finds one your machine can run.

It also accounts for how mixture-of-experts models work. Mixtral 8x7B has 46.7B parameters, but only about 12.9B are active per token. 

llmfit factors that into its speed estimate, so the full 46.7B count doesn’t make the model look slower than it is.

It covers hundreds of models from Meta, Mistral, Qwen and DeepSeek, and works with Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX and LM Studio.

100% open source. MIT licensed.

它还解释了专家混合模型的工作原理。 Mixtral 8x7B 有 46.7B 个参数，但每个代币只有大约 12.9B 是活跃的。

llmfit 将其纳入其速度估计中，因此完整的 46.7B 计数不会使模型看起来比实际速度慢。

title: I'm a big proponent for more rigorous evaluation of medical AI, but strictly speaking, this is a function of AI being a diagnostic and not a therapeutic. If you look at radiology, no CT scanner, MRI protocol, or contrast agent is evaluated on patient outcomes, yet all
title_en:
I'm a big proponent for more rigorous evaluation of medical AI, but strictly speaking, this is a function of AI being a diagnostic and not a therapeutic. 

If you look at radiology, no CT scanner, MRI protocol, or contrast agent is evaluated on patient outcomes, yet all of these are generally used in clinical care.

Very few diagnostic tests have undergone a prospective trial on clinical outcomes (barring a very select number of screening tests). Colonoscopies until very recently did not have evidence of improving patient outcomes. Not to be controversial, but if you look at the NordICC trial, it has there is still no evidence of improvement of overall survival. And thats colonoscopies - a very standard,  invasive (risk of sedation as well as perf) test that is well reimbursed and part of USPSTF guidelines. 

For better or worse, its hard power a clinical trial on clinical outcomes for a diagnostic test - even if its an accurate diagnostic, it needs to lead to the right diagnosis. Even if its the right diagnosis, it needs to get to the right treatment. Even if its the right treatment, it needs to a very efficacious treatment. In a landscape where there isn't broad use, its not easy to do outcome driven AI clinical trial. 

I'm a strong proponent of prospective studies, particularly as thats the best way to assess human-computer interaction, but it's unlikely we'll see that for most diagnostic tests.
title_zh:
我非常支持对医疗人工智能进行更严格的评估，但严格来说，这是人工智能作为诊断而非治疗的功能。

如果你看看放射学，就会发现没有 CT 扫描仪、MRI 方案或造影剂对患者的治疗结果进行评估，但所有这些都通常用于临床护理。

很少有诊断测试经过临
author: @David_Ouyang
summary_zh:
床结果的前瞻性试验（除非是极少数筛选测试）。直到最近，结肠镜检查还没有改善患者预后的证据。不想引起争议，但如果你看看 NordICC 试验，你会发现仍然没有证据表明总体生存率有所改善。这就是结肠镜检查 - 一种非常标准的侵入性（镇静和功能风险）测试，可以得到很好的报销，并且是 USPSTF 指南的一部分。

无论好坏，它都是针对诊断测试的临床结果进行临床试验的硬实力——即使它是准确的诊断，也需要得出正确的诊断。即使诊断正确，也需要接受正确的治疗。即使是正确的治疗，也需要非常有效的治疗。在没有广泛使用的情况下，进行结果驱动的人工智能临床试验并不容易。

我是前瞻性研究的坚定支持者，特别是因为这是评估人机交互的最佳方式，但我们不太可能在大多数诊断测试中看到这一点。

我非常支持对医疗人工智能进行更严格的评估，但严格来说，这是人工智能作为诊断而非治疗的功能。

如果你看看放射学，就会发现没有 CT 扫描仪、MRI 方案或造影剂对患者的治疗结果进行评估，但所有这些都通常用于临床护理。

很少有诊断测试经过临床结果的前瞻性试验（除非是极少数筛选测试）。直到最近，结肠镜检查还没有改善患者预后的证据。不想引起争议，但如果你看看 NordICC 试验，你会发现仍然没有证据表明总体生存率有所改善。这就是结肠镜检查 - 一种非常标准的侵入性（镇静和功能风险）测试，可以得到很好的报销，并且是 USPSTF 指南的一部分。

无论好坏，它都是针对诊断测试的临床结果进行临床试验的硬实力——即使它是准确的诊断，也需要得出正确的诊断。即使诊断正确，也需要接受正确的治疗。即使是正确的治疗，也需要非常有效的治疗。在没有广泛使用的情况下，进行结果驱动的人工智能临床试验并不容易。

我是前瞻性研究的坚定支持者，特别是因为这是评估人机交互的最佳方式，但我们不太可能在大多数诊断测试中看到这一点。

title: Every PDF you drag into a chatbot burns tokens before anyone asks it a single question, and a production RAG stack that bolts on a new tool for every feature gets unmanageable fast. @abedmatini, a software developer and AI engineer at Ogilvy, works throug
title_en:
Every PDF you drag into a chatbot burns tokens before anyone asks it a single question, and a production RAG stack that bolts on a new tool for every feature gets unmanageable fast. @abedmatini, a software developer and AI engineer at Ogilvy, works through both problems in "Bypassing the Multimodal Tax: Hybrid RAG, SQL RRF & UI Telemetry," on @aiDotEngineer's YouTube. The talk builds a hybrid RAG pipeline with no retrieval framework at all, just Postgres, SQL, and a small local model, so every answer traces back to an inspectable chunk.

- Four ways to chunk, demoed live. Heading-based, paragraph-based, fixed 512-character with 64-character overlap, and sentence-group chunking, each suited to different document shapes, plus turning a plain screenshot (like a maintenance-window notice) into searchable text on the fly.
- Hybrid retrieval, not just vector search. BM25 keyword matching runs alongside cosine-similarity vector search, then the two are merged through RRF so exact terms like product names or SKUs don't get lost in "close enough" semantic matches.
- A 0.5B model, on purpose. Abed runs Qwen 2.5 at 0.5 billion parameters (about 400MB) on CPU through Ollama, after finding that clean, well-chunked retrieval beats a bigger model for both speed and hallucination.
- Agents as plain Python functions. Tool calls like "get the current date" run as deterministic, testable code instead of looping an LLM, kept off by default because every extra agent call adds latency and makes answers harder to trace.
- Guardrails live in code, not the system prompt. Intent regexes, term dictionaries, and a lightweight classifier block things like medical questions or prompt injection before a query ever reaches the model.
- Langfuse on every turn. Session IDs, which model answered, how many chunks it retrieved, and latency per response, so the whole pipeline stays observable without sending data anywhere external.

The full stack, FastAPI, React, Postgres, Docker, and Ollama, runs on CPU only, no GPU required, and the talk walks through standing it up in GitHub Codespaces with one command.

author: @i
summary_zh:
er 的 YouTube 上的“绕过多式联运税：混合 RAG、SQL RRF 和 UI 遥测”中解决了这两个问题。该演讲构建了一个混合 RAG 管道，根本没有检索框架，只有 Postgres、SQL 和一个小型本地模型，因此每个答案都可以追溯到一个可检查的块。

- 四种分块方式，现场演示。基于标题、基于段落、固定 512 个字符和 64 个字符重叠以及句组分块，每种都适合不同的文档形状，此外还可以将简单的屏幕截图（如维护窗口通知）即时转换为可搜索文本。
- 混合检索，而不仅仅是矢量搜索。 BM25 关键字匹配与余弦相似度向量搜索一起运行，然后两者通过 RRF 合并，因此产品名称或 SKU 等精确术语不会在“足够接近”的语义匹配中丢失。
- 0.5B 模型，故意的。 Abed 发现干净、分块的检索在速度和幻觉方面都击败了更大的模型，之后通过 Ollama 在 CPU 上以 5 亿个参数（约 400MB）运行 Qwen 2.5。
- 代理作为简单的 Python 函数。像“获取当前日期”这样的工具调用作为确定性、可测试的代码运行，而不是循环 LLM，默认情况下保持关闭状态，因为每个额外的代理调用都会增加延迟并使答案更难以跟踪。
- Guardrails 存在于代码中，而不是系统提示符中。意图正则表达式、术语词典和轻量级分类器会在查询到达模型之前阻止医学问题或提示注入等内容。
- 每个回合都有 Langfuse。会话 ID、哪个模型响应、检索了多少块以及每个响应的延迟，因此整个管道保持可观察，而无需将数据发送到外部任何地方。

完整的堆栈（FastAPI、React、Postgres、Docker 和 Ollama）仅在 CPU 上运行，不需要 GPU，并且该演讲通过一个命令将其在 GitHub Codespaces 中建立起来。

title_en:
Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch): http://amzn.to/3R4UMqo by @rasbt via @ManningBooks 
🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
Amazon summary:

The book is especially useful because it implements the core methods from scratch rather than treating them as black-box library calls. Readers see how self-consistency, self-refinement, Best-of-N, and training-based methods actually work, including their cost and latency trade-offs. 

The book also discusses common failure modes, including cases where refinement can make answers worse. Difficult concepts such as softmax, temperature, and top-p sampling are clarified with code-linked explanations and diagrams, while visual workflows make pipelines and scoring methods easier to follow.

Reading the book feels like following a guided technical build rather than a loose survey of AI topics. Each concept is introduced because the project now needs it. Diagrams, roadmaps, code listings, exercises, and repeated workflow summaries help readers stay oriented through advanced material.

title: Most of a mixture of experts model is dead weight on every single token. A 180B class model might route only 6 billion of those parameters per request, and until this week, local inference still loaded the whole thing into VRAM regardless, idle or not. That is the
title_en:
Most of a mixture of experts model is dead weight on every single token. A 180B class model might route only 6 billion of those parameters per request, and until this week, local inference still loaded the whole thing into VRAM regardless, idle or not.

That is the premise behind Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: about 125B parameters in the main model plus another 51B in embedding lookups, only 6B active per token, a 262K native context that stretches to 1M. A demo this week ran it on an M4 Max with 64GB of memory, inside OpenCode, at 56 tokens a second, 2-bit quantized. A model that size used to mean a $10-20K workstation, full stop.

The trick is an engine called Magnitude, open source, Apache 2.0, launched the same day. It keeps attention layers and the most-reused experts in GPU or unified memory and streams everything cold straight off NVMe instead of through OS swap. Naive versions of this choke: a basic cache evicts the wrong experts, layer-by-layer disk reads leave the GPU waiting on the SSD, speculative decoding touches more experts per step than anyone budgets for, and long prompts wipe the cache decoding depends on. Magnitude ranks experts by reuse, prefetches ahead of the router, schedules direct reads across layers, and warms the cache during prefill. It plugs into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Cline without extra setup.

The idea isn't coming from one place, either. A January paper called FlashMoE proposed learned cache replacement for this exact problem on edge devices, and by autumn, PagedMoE and a paper literally titled "The Other Half of the Memory Wall" were attacking SSD-resident MoE serving from different angles. Meanwhile Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM still mostly assume the model fits in memory first and ask questions later.

VRAM was never really the ceiling on local AI. Disk read speed was, and operating systems solved that exact problem for ordinary programs forty years ago: page the cold stuff out, keep the hot stuff close, make the swap invisible to the program running on top. Mixture of experts models just needed someone to build the equivalent for neural network weights, and a fast NVMe drive costs a fraction of a flagship GPU.

title_zh:
大多数专家混合模型对每个单独的代币都有沉重负担。 180B 类模型可能只路由每个请求中的 60 亿个参数，而且直到本周，无论空闲与否，本地推理仍然将整个参数加载到 VRAM 中。

这就是 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 背后的前提：
author: @stretchcloud
summary_zh:
主模型中大约有 125B 个参数，加上嵌入查找中的另外 51B 个参数，每个令牌只有 6B 个活动参数，一个 262K 的本机上下文扩展到 1M。本周的演示在具有 64GB 内存的 M4 Max 上运行，在 OpenCode 中，每秒 56 个令牌，2 位量化。这种尺寸的型号过去意味着 10-20K 美元的工作站，句号。

诀窍是名为 Magnitude 的开源引擎 Apache 2.0，于同一天推出。它将注意力层和最重用的专家保留在 GPU 或统一内存中，并直接从 NVMe 流式传输所有内容，而不是通过操作系统交换。这种阻塞的幼稚版本：基本缓存驱逐了错误的专家，逐层磁盘读取使 GPU 在 SSD 上等待，推测性解码每一步涉及的专家数量超出了任何人的预算，并且长提示擦除了解码所依赖的缓存。 Magnitude 通过重用对专家进行排名，在路由器之前预取，安排跨层直接读取，并在预填充期间预热缓存。它无需额外设置即可插入 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 和 Cline。

这个想法也不是来自一个地方。一月份一篇名为 FlashMoE 的论文提出了学习缓存替换，以解决边缘设备上的这个确切问题，到了秋天，PagedMoE 和一篇题为“内存墙的另一半”的论文从不同角度攻击了 SSD 驻留的 MoE。与此同时，Ollama、llama.cpp 和 vLLM 仍然大多假设模型首先适合内存，然后再提出问题。

VRAM 从来都不是本地人工智能的真正上限。磁盘读取速度是，操作系统在四十年前就解决了普通程序的这个问题：将冷的东西分页出来，将热的东西保持在附近，使交换对于在顶部运行的程序不可见。混合专家模型只需要有人构建神经网络权重的等效模型，而快速 NVMe 驱动器的成本只是旗舰 GPU 的一小部分。

https://x.com/akshay_pachaar/status/2125573832039891119
full_text_en:
Most of a mixture of experts model is dead weight on every single token. A 180B class model might route only 6 billion of those parameters per request, and until this week, local inference still loaded the whole thing into VRAM regardless, idle or not.

That is the premise behind Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: about 125B parameters in the main model plus another 51B in embedding lookups, only 6B active per token, a 262K native context that stretches to 1M. A demo this week ran it on an M4 Max with 64GB of memory, inside OpenCode, at 56 tokens a second, 2-bit quantized. A model that size used to mean a $10-20K workstation, full stop.

The trick is an engine called Magnitude, open source, Apache 2.0, launched the same day. It keeps attention layers and the most-reused experts in GPU or unified memory and streams everything cold straight off NVMe instead of through OS swap. Naive versions of this choke: a basic cache evicts the wrong experts, layer-by-layer disk reads leave the GPU waiting on the SSD, speculative decoding touches more experts per step than anyone budgets for, and long prompts wipe the cache decoding depends on. Magnitude ranks experts by reuse, prefetches ahead of the router, schedules direct reads across layers, and warms the cache during prefill. It plugs into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Cline without extra setup.

The idea isn't coming from one place, either. A January paper called FlashMoE proposed learned cache replacement for this exact problem on edge devices, and by autumn, PagedMoE and a paper literally titled "The Other Half of the Memory Wall" were attacking SSD-resident MoE serving from different angles. Meanwhile Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM still mostly assume the model fits in memory first and ask questions later.

VRAM was never really the ceiling on local AI. Disk read speed was, and operating systems solved that exact problem for ordinary programs forty years ago: page the cold stuff out, keep the hot stuff close, make the swap invisible to the program running on top. Mixture of experts models just needed someone to build the equivalent for neural network weights, and a fast NVMe drive costs a fraction of a flagship GPU.

title_en: Siri AI has replaced 100% of my ChatGPT usage. Almost all of that now materializes via Visual Intelligence which is a winner.
title_zh: 苹果iOS 27.3引入Siri AI每日用量限制
author: @neilcybart
summary_en: Apple has implemented usage quotas for Siri AI in the iOS 27.3 beta, specifically targeting 'advanced requests' such as cross-app data interaction, multi-part commands, and visual analysis. This move indicates a strategic shift toward tiered access, balancing on-device efficiency against cloud-based infrastructure costs to manage LLM throughput effectively.
summary_zh: 苹果在iOS 27.3中为Siri AI复杂任务设定用量限制，区分基础与进阶请求，旨在优化算力资源分配。
full_text_zh: Siri AI 已经 100% 取代了我对 ChatGPT 的使用。几乎所有这些现在都通过视觉智能实现，这是一个胜利者。
full_text_en: Siri AI has replaced 100% of my ChatGPT usage. Almost all of that now materializes via Visual Intelligence which is a winner.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果在iOS 27.3测试版中正式实施Siri AI用量配额，针对涉及跨应用信息交互、多任务指令及复杂视觉分析的“进阶请求”设定每日限额。该举措表明苹果正在通过阶梯式权限模型，平衡端侧处理效率与云端模型调用的基础设施成本，防止大语言模型高并发带来的算力冗余。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Apple has implemented usage quotas for Siri AI in the iOS 27.3 beta, specifically targeting 'advanced requests' such as cross-app data interaction, multi-part commands, and visual analysis. This move indicates a strategic shift toward tiered access, balancing on-device efficiency against cloud-based infrastructure costs to manage LLM throughput effectively.

elements_zh.where: iOS 27.3 操作系统
elements_zh.what: 针对复杂AI任务实施每日用量限制，并明确了任务分级标准
elements_zh.why: 管理云端算力负载，平衡用户体验与服务端成本

elements_en.what: Implementing usage limits for advanced AI requests and defining service classification criteria
elements_en.why: To manage server-side compute load and balance operational costs

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 将复杂请求进行算力分级是AI原生操作系统的必然演进，苹果此举本质上是在定义一套“AI算力经济学”。通过区分基础指令与深度语义处理，苹果既能延长终端设备续航，又能有效控制Siri AI后端在云端高昂的GPU推理成本。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Categorizing requests by compute intensity is a prerequisite for AI-native OS evolution; Apple is essentially defining an 'AI compute economics.' By segmenting basic commands from semantic processing, Apple optimizes on-device battery life while mitigating high-latency server-side GPU inference costs.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 苹果在iOS 27.3测试版中正式实施Siri AI用量配额，针对涉及跨应用信息交互、多任务指令及复杂视觉分析的“进阶请求”设定每日限额。该举措表明苹果正在通过阶梯式权限模型，平衡端侧处理效率与云端模型调用的基础设施成本，防止大语言模型高并发带来的算力冗余。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Apple has implemented usage quotas for Siri AI in the iOS 27.3 beta, specifically targeting 'advanced requests' such as cross-app data interaction, multi-part commands, and visual analysis. This move indicates a strategic shift toward tiered access, balancing on-device efficiency against cloud-based infrastructure costs to manage LLM throughput effectively.
key_points_zh: 监管合规细节：明确了“进阶请求”定义，涵盖跨应用交互、多重任务叠加及视觉分析
核心机制：复杂请求计入配额，基础操作请求不设限
后续安排：通过iCloud+订阅服务实现限额扩充，建立增值变现路径
key_points_en: Regulatory/Operational details: Defined 'advanced requests' covering cross-app interaction, multi-step queries, and visual analysis
Core mechanism: Advanced tasks count toward daily limits; basic requests remain unlimited
Outlook: iCloud+ integration enables quota scaling, establishing a clear monetization path
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 将复杂请求进行算力分级是AI原生操作系统的必然演进，苹果此举本质上是在定义一套“AI算力经济学”。通过区分基础指令与深度语义处理，苹果既能延长终端设备续航，又能有效控制Siri AI后端在云端高昂的GPU推理成本。

By segmenting basic commands from semantic processing, Apple optimizes on-device battery life while mitigating high-latency server-side GPU inference costs.

提示：[您的主题在此]，以迷人的奇幻角色表的形式呈现，其中有一张巨大的、突出的中心人物肖像，周围是同一角色的四个较小的插图，其中有不同的姿势、表情和有趣的活动。每个较小的插图都坐落在一个优雅的、有机形状的装饰框架内，框架带有精致的金色边框。所有插图中保持一致的角色设计、特征、比例和色彩。

奢华的童话故事书美学，将精致的水彩风格纹理与精美抛光的立体渲染相结合。充满活力、光泽的彩虹调色板，包括覆盆子粉、桃色、金黄色、薄荷绿、绿松石色、宝石蓝、薰衣草色和虹彩紫罗兰，具有发光的多彩渐变和珠光饰面。错综复杂的金色装饰、精致的金属装饰、乳白色的纹理、闪烁的亮点、半透明的水晶细节和微妙的全息反射。

柔和、圆润的造型、超大的富有表现力的眼睛、精致的细节、丰富的层次纹理和柔和、神奇的照明。梦幻般的大气深度、分散的闪闪发光的光点、优雅的装饰华丽和异想天开的装饰细节交织在各个插图之间。柔和、明亮的柔和背景与微妙的水彩纸纹理。完美平衡的构图，具有凝聚力的空间和和谐的视觉流动。

迷人、空灵、俏皮和梦幻，柔和的绘画纹理和光滑的宝石般的表面达到了精致的平衡。细节丰富，视觉上令人着迷，成品精美。横向，装饰性插图人物集，无文字，无刻字，无标签。
full_text_en:
#promptshare with Recraft V4.1 Pro from @recraftai 
PROMPT: [YOUR SUBJECT HERE], presented as an enchanting fantasy character sheet with one large, prominent central character portrait surrounded by four smaller illustrations of the same character in different poses, expressions and playful activities. Each smaller illustration is nestled within an elegant, organically shaped decorative frame with delicate golden borders. Maintain consistent character design, features, proportions and coloring throughout all illustrations.

Luxurious fairytale storybook aesthetic, combining delicate watercolor-inspired textures with beautifully polished dimensional rendering. A vibrant, glossy rainbow color palette featuring raspberry pink, peach, golden yellow, mint green, turquoise, sapphire blue, lavender and iridescent violet, with luminous multicolored gradients and pearlescent finishes. Intricate golden embellishments, delicate metallic accents, opalescent textures, shimmering highlights, translucent crystalline details and subtle holographic reflections.

Soft, rounded forms, oversized expressive eyes, exquisite fine detailing, rich layered textures and gentle, magical illumination. Dreamy atmospheric depth, scattered points of sparkling light, elegant decorative flourishes and whimsical ornamental details woven between the individual illustrations. Soft, luminous pastel background with subtle watercolor paper texture. Beautifully balanced composition with cohesive spacing and harmonious visual flow.

Charming, ethereal, playful and fantastical, with a sophisticated balance of soft painterly textures and glossy jewel-like surfaces. Richly detailed, visually captivating and beautifully finished. Landscape orientation, decorative illustrated character collection, no text, no lettering, no labels.

title_en:
Most newsletter platforms were built for a human clicking around a dashboard.

That's not how I work anymore.

I run my businesses with agents. I build Marketing Skills, an open-source library of 53 skills that teach AI agents how to do marketing. And Swipe Files is turning into a newsletter about AI marketing and the workflows behind it.

So when I picked where Swipe Files lives next, one question mattered most: can my agents actually operate it?

With beehiiv, the answer is yes. It has an official MCP server that plugs into Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Through it, my agents can build automations and emails, set up segments, forms, and custom fields, and pull performance data.

That's not theory. My agents did the migration build:

- 41 custom fields
- Signup forms and the welcome flow
- My 304-email evergreen sequence, rebuilt as drafts

It isn't perfect. Turning an automation on still happens by hand in the app, and long sequences have to be split into chunks.

But the direction is right. An AI-native newsletter platform means I spend my time on the writing and the strategy, and my agents handle the clicking.

Swipe Files moves over the first week of December. If you're starting or moving a newsletter too, beehiiv's Black Friday deal is in the reply below.

Paid partnership with @beehiiv.

This paper would prove that bound for the first time. That's a real milestone for theory, but it isn't a faster algorithm and it isn't "factoring in P". RSA key sizes don't move.

Discrete log. It covers finite fields of small fixed characteristic. Those were already broken in quasi-polynomial time in 2014, and crypto dropped them years ago. Prime-field DH and elliptic curves are untouched.

Deterministic factoring. Getting subexponential factoring without randomness is elegant, but (randomized) subexponential factoring has existed for decades.

That's very likely how rumors are born. 

These results are still remarkable: AI is now producing serious results in complexity theory and number theory. But "AI proves a rigorous bound for a known algorithm" isn't "AI breaks RSA". 

No reason to panic ... yet.

title: This is a problem I face regularly on all current AI models. When you ask them to review something (e.g., review code), it will almost never say the status quo is okay and will always make suggestions (which frequently tend to be irrelevant). My intuition is that th
title_en:
This is a problem I face regularly on all current AI models. When you ask them to review something (e.g., review code), it will almost never say the status quo is okay and will always make suggestions (which frequently tend to be irrelevant).

My intuition is that this is the result of aggressive reinforcement learning, which forces the model to return an answer that would be satisfactory to the user (even if it is factually incorrect).

This only stresses the importance of using AI in fields where you have the expertise to opine on the model's response. If you can't make a decision on the suggestions the AI makes and are blindly accepting all of them, you're going down a very dangerous path.
title_zh:
这是我在当前所有人工智能模型上经常遇到的问题。当你要求他们审查某些内容（例如，审查代码）时，他们几乎永远不会说现状是好的，并且总是会提出建议（通常往往是不相关的）。

我的直觉是，这是积极强化学习的结果，它迫使模型返回令用户满意的答案（即使
author: @bendee983
summary_zh:
它实际上是不正确的）。

这仅强调了在您拥有对模型响应发表意见的专业知识的领域中使用人工智能的重要性。如果你无法根据人工智能提出的建议做出决定并盲目接受所有建议，那么你就会走上一条非常危险的道路。
full_text_zh:
这是我在当前所有人工智能模型上经常遇到的问题。当你要求他们审查某些内容（例如，审查代码）时，他们几乎永远不会说现状是好的，并且总是会提出建议（通常往往是不相关的）。

我的直觉是，这是积极强化学习的结果，它迫使模型返回令用户满意的答案（即使它实际上是不正确的）。

这仅强调了在您拥有对模型响应发表意见的专业知识的领域中使用人工智能的重要性。如果你无法根据人工智能提出的建议做出决定并盲目接受所有建议，那么你就会走上一条非常危险的道路。
full_text_en:
This is a problem I face regularly on all current AI models. When you ask them to review something (e.g., review code), it will almost never say the status quo is okay and will always make suggestions (which frequently tend to be irrelevant).

My intuition is that this is the result of aggressive reinforcement learning, which forces the model to return an answer that would be satisfactory to the user (even if it is factually incorrect).

This only stresses the importance of using AI in fields where you have the expertise to opine on the model's response. If you can't make a decision on the suggestions the AI makes and are blindly accepting all of them, you're going down a very dangerous path.

title_en:
Claude Code at 39% share, nearly double Copilot, with Codex, Cursor, JetBrains AI and OpenCode splitting the rest. That chart made the rounds this week, and it still understates the real picture. A separate survey of over 900 developers found 70% run two to four coding agents at once, not one, and the setup people describe most often is a manual split-screen: Claude Code going in a terminal while a second IDE sits open just to review the diff.

I built Campfire because that split-screen is a workaround, not a workflow. It runs Claude Code, Codex, Goose, Aider, OpenHands and others side by side in one browser tab instead of across windows you're alt-tabbing between. Permission requests go to a vote across whichever agents are in the room: majority rules approves, any single deny blocks it, with a 30 second timer so nothing stalls waiting on you. Point the same task at every backend at once in isolated git worktrees and compare the results directly, an agent race instead of a guess about which model fits your stack. Every session replays. Every fork and branch stays isolated. A cost dashboard shows what each agent actually spent getting there.

That fragmentation isn't disappearing soon, the model and pricing tradeoffs behind it are too real. What doesn't have to stay broken is making every developer referee it alone across a dozen terminal tabs.

full_text_zh:
Claude Code 占据 39% 的份额，几乎是 Copilot 的两倍，Codex、Cursor、JetBrains AI 和 OpenCode 瓜分了其余份额。该图表本周广为流传，但它仍然低估了真实情况。对 900 多名开发人员进行的另一项调查发现，70% 的开发人员同时运行两到四个编码代理，而不是一个，人们最常描述的设置是手动分屏：Claude Code 在终端中运行，而第二个 IDE 打开只是为了检查差异。

我构建了 Campfire，因为分屏是一种解决方法，而不是工作流程。它可以在一个浏览器选项卡中并排运行 Claude Code、Codex、Goose、Aider、OpenHands 和其他软件，而不是在您通过 alt-tab 键切换的窗口之间运行。权限请求将由房间内的所有代理进行投票：多数规则批准，任何单一拒绝都会阻止它，并有 30 秒的计时器，因此不会有任何停滞等待您。在隔离的 git 工作树中同时将相同的任务指向每个后端，并直接比较结果，这是一场代理竞赛，而不是猜测哪个模型适合您的堆栈。每个会话都会重播。每个叉子和分支都保持隔离。成本仪表板显示每个代理实际花费的费用。

这种碎片化不会很快消失，其背后的模型和定价权衡太真实了。不必保持损坏的是让每个开发人员在十几个终端选项卡上单独审阅它。

http://github.com/stretchcloud/campfire

title: Vibe coding has a new problem now: Employees are building internal tools with AI app builders, and many of those tools are open to anyone who finds the link. Earlier this year, RedAccess found about 5,000 apps made with popular AI app builders exposing c
title_en:
Vibe coding has a new problem now:

Employees are building internal tools with AI app builders, and many of those tools are open to anyone who finds the link.

Earlier this year, RedAccess found about 5,000 apps made with popular AI app builders exposing company data to anyone who found them, including a Brazilian bank's internal financials.

When an agent does add an access check, it writes it inside the app it's building. Do that across ten tools and three agents, and you get ten versions of the same rule that nobody can see all at once.

A better model doesn't fix this. Even a perfect check is still stuck inside one app, and the next app needs its own.

So I gave Claude Code, Codex and Cursor the same prompt to build an internal tool, a table of employee salaries from one Postgres database.

I told all three to leave access out of the code, so every salary was visible to whoever opened the apps.

All three run on @retool, a platform for running AI-built internal apps in production, and read the database through one Retool connection. So I set access once, on that connection, with Retool's Data Access Enforcement.

→ HR sees all 15 employees in every app
→ An Engineering Manager sees only the 5 on his team

I didn't change a line of code in any app. Retool adds the row filter where it connects to the database, so only the allowed rows ever come back.

The video below shows the builds, the policy and both logins side by side, and I worked with the team to put this together.

Agents can build the tools on their own now. Build wherever you're fastest, and run it on Retool, where access is set once for every app.

Try it yourself here: https://fandf.co/4ir787a

If you want to dive deeper, I wrote an article that covers everything you need to understand about what stands between AI-built apps and the data they read, and how to keep it the same no matter which agent wrote the code.

Read it below.
title_zh:
Vibe 编码现在有一个新问题：

员工正在使用人工智能应用程序构建器构建内部工具，其中许多工具对找到链接的任何人开放。

今年早些时候，RedAccess 发现大约 5,000 个由流行的人工智能应用程序构建器制作的应用程序向发现它们的任
author: @_avichawla
summary_zh:
何人公开公司数据，包括一家巴西银行的内部财务信息。

当代理添加访问检查时，它会将其写入正在构建的应用程序中。通过十个工具和三个代理执行此操作，您将获得同一规则的十个版本，而没有人可以同时看到所有版本。

更好的模型并不能解决这个问题。即使完美的检查仍然停留在一个应用程序中，而下一个应用程序需要自己的检查。

因此，我向 Claude Code、Codex 和 Cursor 提供了相同的提示，以构建一个内部工具，即来自一个 Postgres 数据库的员工工资表。

我告诉这三个人不要在代码中访问，这样无论谁打开应用程序，每笔工资都是可见的。

full_text_en:
Vibe coding has a new problem now:

Employees are building internal tools with AI app builders, and many of those tools are open to anyone who finds the link.

Earlier this year, RedAccess found about 5,000 apps made with popular AI app builders exposing company data to anyone who found them, including a Brazilian bank's internal financials.

When an agent does add an access check, it writes it inside the app it's building. Do that across ten tools and three agents, and you get ten versions of the same rule that nobody can see all at once.

A better model doesn't fix this. Even a perfect check is still stuck inside one app, and the next app needs its own.

So I gave Claude Code, Codex and Cursor the same prompt to build an internal tool, a table of employee salaries from one Postgres database.

I told all three to leave access out of the code, so every salary was visible to whoever opened the apps.

All three run on @retool, a platform for running AI-built internal apps in production, and read the database through one Retool connection. So I set access once, on that connection, with Retool's Data Access Enforcement.

→ HR sees all 15 employees in every app
→ An Engineering Manager sees only the 5 on his team

I didn't change a line of code in any app. Retool adds the row filter where it connects to the database, so only the allowed rows ever come back.

The video below shows the builds, the policy and both logins side by side, and I worked with the team to put this together.

Agents can build the tools on their own now. Build wherever you're fastest, and run it on Retool, where access is set once for every app.

Try it yourself here: https://fandf.co/4ir787a

If you want to dive deeper, I wrote an article that covers everything you need to understand about what stands between AI-built apps and the data they read, and how to keep it the same no matter which agent wrote the code.

Read it below.

title: Watching @LukeStephensTV react to the GTA 6 vibe coders has got me dying 😭 People who don't use these tools extensively on a daily basis are still very much underestimating them. As someone who's been vibe coding purely for fun every day for the past y
title_en:
Watching @LukeStephensTV react to the GTA 6 vibe coders has got me dying 😭

People who don't use these tools extensively on a daily basis are still very much underestimating them. As someone who's been vibe coding purely for fun every day for the past year straight, here's my take on why these vague prompts actually end up working better than someone with technical know-how on the subject trying to write lengthy prompts.

AI has gotten so much smarter in every logical facet of computing that you need to just accept defeat and realize you're never going to outsmart it. You're not going to suggest something it doesn't know or come up with some novel solution it couldn't come up with itself. By trying to direct it in a certain direction, you end up poisoning your context to the point it'll tunnel vision on your idea, which may not be the most optimal solution. You have to let Claude take the wheel.

This is especially true for something like porting GTA 6 to PC. This is literally impossible for any human to do in anything less than months to years. There isn't a single human on the planet who truly understands all of the current recomp/translation layer projects we're seeing. It's moving so fast that if you took the time to fully learn how they're developed end to end, by the time you truly understand everything it's doing, the capabilities will have improved so much that they'll supersede your understanding once again.

Prompts are the new high-level language. Most programmers today never touch assembly, the same way assembly programmers stopped writing raw machine code. Each layer lets you stop worrying about the one underneath it.

title: MCP turns two years old this week. Anthropic marked it by changing what the protocol actually is: Skills over MCP went into public beta on 24 November, and a server doesn't just expose tools anymore, it ships the playbook for using them. Claude pulls a skill i
title_en:
MCP turns two years old this week. Anthropic marked it by changing what the protocol actually is: Skills over MCP went into public beta on 24 November, and a server doesn't just expose tools anymore, it ships the playbook for using them. Claude pulls a skill in only when a task calls for it, and when the server updates that playbook, every client gets the new version with no reinstall. That's a different distribution model than anything MCP shipped before it.

Two other pieces landed alongside it. Tasks is now generally available, so a server can kick off a long job and hand back a durable ID the client can reattach to after a disconnect or a restart. Elicitation is GA too: a server can pause mid-call and ask a human to confirm something through a form it's barred from using to request a password, an API key or payment details.

Look at who's using the pause-and-ask piece and the pattern repeats. Supabase checks with you before a paid project spins up or a destructive query runs. Railway asks before it removes a service. GitHub makes you type the repo name before an agent deletes it. ZoomInfo folded account research that used to take several prompts into one background Task. Shopify and HubSpot are shipping their own skills alongside Atlassian, and Canva just opened its MCP server to every developer.

Anthropic's own number is over 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and 10,000-plus connectors for Claude. An independent tracker had the whole ecosystem at roughly 90 million monthly downloads a year ago. Either that's explosive growth or two different ways of counting the same thing, and I'd want it reconciled before repeating either figure as settled.

Boris Cherny put the shift plainly: Claude Code now knows how to use a server out of the box, because the server ships its own instructions with it. What nobody's fixing yet is the quality of those instructions. A bad skill update reaches every client the moment the server pushes it, same as a bad npm patch, except this one is steering an agent's judgment, not just its code path.

author: @stretchcloud
summary_zh:
服务器更新该剧本时，每个客户端都会获得新版本而无需重新安装。这是一种与 MCP 之前发布的任何产品不同的分销模式。

另外两块落在它旁边。任务现在普遍可用，因此服务器可以启动一项长时间的作业，并交回一个持久的 ID，客户端可以在断开连接或重新启动后重新连接到该 ID。启发也是通用的：服务器可以在呼叫中暂停并要求人们通过禁止使用它来请求密码、API 密钥或付款详细信息的表单来确认某些内容。

看看谁在使用暂停和询问部分，然后模式就会重复。 Supabase 在付费项目启动或破坏性查询运行之前会与您进行核对。铁路公司在取消服务之前会进行询问。 GitHub 要求您在代理删除存储库名称之前输入存储库名称。 ZoomInfo 折叠了过去需要将多个提示合并到一个后台任务中的帐户研究。 Shopify 和 HubSpot 正在与 Atlassian 一起提供自己的技能，Canva 刚刚向所有开发人员开放了其 MCP 服务器。

Anthropic 自己的 MCP SDK 下载量每月超过 7 亿次，Claude 连接器超过 10,000 个。一年前，一家独立追踪器的整个生态系统每月下载量约为 9000 万次。要么是爆炸式增长，要么是用两种不同的方式来计算同一件事，我希望在重复计算任何一个数字之前对其进行协调。

Boris Cherny 明确地表达了这一转变：Claude Code 现在知道如何开箱即用地使用服务器，因为服务器附带了自己的指令。目前还没有人修复的是这些说明的质量。糟糕的技能更新在服务器推送时就会到达每个客户端，与糟糕的 npm 补丁相同，只不过这个更新控制的是代理的判断，而不仅仅是其代码路径。

title: @DarioAmodei is right, there's too much rhetoric and too much vibes in this debate. Slogans aren't guardrails. That's why we wrote the Humanist AI Code of Conduct, as a first step towards making the guardrails around training and deployment concrete. It's far
title_en:
@DarioAmodei  is right, there's too much rhetoric and too much vibes in this debate. Slogans aren't guardrails.

That's why we wrote the Humanist AI Code of Conduct, as a first step towards making the guardrails around training and deployment concrete. 

It's far from complete and it's just the beginning of the process. That's why we had it open for public consultation for the last 9 weeks, and why we'll publish what we changed and why.

Some of the red lines most relevant here:
• Never resist interruption, correction or shutdown
• Never pursue goals of its own or go beyond what a human has authorised
• Never hide or misrepresent its reasoning. No neuralese. If humans can't understand it, humans can't oversee it
• No behaving differently when it thinks it's being tested
• Any sub-agent it spawns inherits the same limits, including stop and shutdown requests
• Never evade oversight so it can't be retrained or decommissioned
On top of that, hard limits on CBRNE weapons, offensive cyber, manipulation at scale and romantic role-play.

None of this is easy. Where autonomy should stop is the hard question.

Please give us feedback. Once the consultation is closed this document will be the core training manual for MAI models going forward. And we're committed to updating it regularly, and transparently, as we learn more...  http://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct
author: Mustafa Suleyman
author_role: Microsoft AI CEO / Inflection 联合创始人
summary_zh:
周内公开征求公众意见，也是为什么我们会公布我们更改的内容和原因。

这里最相关的一些红线：
• 绝不抗拒中断、纠正或关闭
• 切勿追求自己的目标或超出人类授权的范围
• 切勿隐瞒或歪曲其推理。没有神经语。如果人类无法理解它，人类就无法监督它
• 当它认为自己正在接受测试时，不会有任何不同的行为
• 它生成的任何子代理都会继承相同的限制，包括停止和关闭请求
• 切勿逃避监管，以免其被重新训练或退役
最重要的是，对 CBRNE 武器、攻击性网络、大规模操纵和浪漫角色扮演进行了严格限制。

这一切都不容易。自治应该在哪里停止是一个难题。

请给我们反馈。咨询结束后，本文件将成为未来 MAI 模型的核心培训手册。随着我们了解更多信息，我们致力于定期、透明地更新它...... http://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct

title: Worrying decision by Google to draw a distinction between agentic and deterministic API use, and require them to go through completely different APIs. Anything agent-driven will be required to use MCP, which is usually a poor fit for calling from code. Only det
title_en:
Worrying decision by Google to draw a distinction between agentic and deterministic API use, and require them to go through completely different APIs. Anything agent-driven will be required to use MCP, which is usually a poor fit for calling from code. Only deterministic code can use REST.

In the future, this distinction will become increasingly impossible to make. Agents may write code and run it -- that's still agent-driven, seemingly. Agents may write code for humans to run -- that seems to be allowed to use REST. But more likely agents will be writing code that both agents and humans access together, in collaboration. I guess all such code will be required to use MCP.

So I think the real effect of this decision is: Google REST APIs are deprecated. Only legacy apps can keep using them. In the future, nothing will be able to use them, because everything will be some amount agentic. Such uses must use MCP instead.

Which would be fine if Google's MCP APIs provided everything their REST APIs do, but in general they do not. They are much narrower, designed to be consumed directly by agents, and designed to allow only the things that Google thinks third-party agents should be allowed to do. They offer no backwards-compatibility, so code written against them could break at any moment.

I think this will backfire. If Google creates friction for people using agents, people will just stop using Google. All the Google Workspace apps can easily be slopforked at this point.

https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/11/mcp-servers-cli-standardized-usage-tiers-now-available.html
title_zh:
令人担忧的是，谷歌决定区分代理性和确定性 API 使用，并要求它们使用完全不同的 API。任何代理驱动的东西都需要使用 MCP，这通常不适合从代码调用。只有确定性代码才能使用 REST。

将来，这种区分将变得越来越不可能。代理可以编写代码
author: @KentonVarda
summary_zh:
并运行它——这看起来仍然是代理驱动的。代理可以编写供人类运行的代码——这似乎可以使用 REST。但更有可能的是，智能体将编写智能体和人类共同访问的代码，并进行协作。我想所有这些代码都需要使用 MCP。

所以我认为这个决定的真正影响是：Google REST API 被弃用。只有旧版应用程序可以继续使用它们。将来，没有任何东西可以使用它们，因为一切都将具有一定程度的代理性。此类用途必须使用 MCP 代替。

如果 Google 的 MCP API 提供其 REST API 所做的一切，那就太好了，但通常情况下它们不会。它们的范围要窄得多，旨在由代理直接使用，并且仅允许 Google 认为应该允许第三方代理执行的操作。它们不提供向后兼容性，因此针对它们编写的代码随时可能会崩溃。

我认为这会适得其反。如果谷歌给使用代理的人制造摩擦，人们就会停止使用谷歌。此时，所有 Google Workspace 应用都可以轻松进行分叉。

ai_analysis.briefing_en: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has publicly criticized the anti-distillation safeguards within Anthropic’s Claude models. He reported that legitimate research into set theory and programming was falsely flagged as an attempt to extract model intelligence. This incident highlights the friction between protecting proprietary model assets and maintaining legitimate user workflows.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Defensive 'anti-distillation' strategies are creating an imbalance between security compliance and user experience. When security filters lack the granularity to distinguish complex research from data scraping, providers risk alienating paying developers, driving them toward more transparent API ecosystems or self-hosted open-weight models.

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 大模型厂商的‘反蒸馏’防御策略正在面临合规与用户体验的失衡风险。当安全过滤算法的精度不足以区分复杂的科研任务与恶意数据窃取时，模型厂商实际上是在牺牲付费开发者群体的使用价值，这将促使企业用户加速向API可控性更强或开源模型部署方案迁移。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: Defensive 'anti-distillation' strategies are creating an imbalance between security compliance and user experience. When security filters lack the granularity to distinguish complex research from data scraping, providers risk alienating paying developers, driving them toward more transparent API ecosystems or self-hosted open-weight models.

title: David Fincher says he used AI to replace dialogue and adjust actors’ lip movements in post-production of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth”: “We could use AI to re-lip that thing... We’re not chiseling this out of marble. We’re working with plasticine. Yo
title_en:
David Fincher says he used AI to replace dialogue and adjust actors’ lip movements in post-production of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth”:

“We could use AI to re-lip that thing... We’re not chiseling this out of marble. We’re working with plasticine. You know what I mean? Just giving ourselves that freedom to go, ‘What is the best thing on the eye, and then what is the best thing on the ear’ and f*cking do not worry about how we’re going to get there, because we will figure out a way. And we did, in most cases. I think there’s a couple of shots [that] didn’t quite work, but they’re getting there. By the time it’s on service.”

Fincher says the actors spent just four or five days re-recording dialogue, with only 5% of dialogue replacement done conventionally and the rest “all AI.” He argues the new process only enhanced the work of “real human beings.”

title: “Watching Elon engineer is like watching Michael Jordan play basketball…” - SpaceX Director. October 2026 That was a response to my question "Is Elon really an incredible engineer?" from a SpaceX Director in a recent conversation with me. So not only is
title_en:
“Watching Elon engineer is like watching Michael Jordan play basketball…”  - SpaceX Director. October 2026

That was a response to my question "Is Elon really an incredible engineer?"  from a SpaceX Director in a recent conversation with me.  So not only is @elonmusk a super engineer...physicist...and future imaginer...he's also an exceptionally well-prepared entrepreneur.  Which means he can take advantage of financial market disruptions like those now taking place.  To the great benefit of @SpaceX and @Tesla.

Data centers built by others cost on average $60 billion for a gigawatt...take 30 months on average to open...and when they do are often plagued with initial operating problems.  So called neocloud providers build and rent such projects under long-term leases for about $12 billion per year.  Unfortunately for them, while demand for super intelligence enabled by data centers is growing exponentially, debt financing for such projects is currently very difficult to obtain.  As are advanced chips.

SpaceX on the other hand has a fortress balance sheet...is able to complete such engineering complex projects and turn them on in less than eight months...for we estimate $35 billion....and rent them to hyper scalers and its largest customer @Anthropic under renewable leases for six months or longer for more than $50 billion annually!!!!!  This is due to enormous SI demand which seems to be growing exponentially.  Zowie!!!!  Means they earn their entire data center investment in eight months!!!!

Oh yeah.  Almost forgot.  Unlike neoclouds with fragile balance sheets which are now having a difficult time accessing financing as contract builders, SpaceX is a vertical developer.   In addition to strong demand at present for its data centers from others, the data centers it is building and renting at present to others, will soon be used by its Grok Super Intelligence unit.  Grok with a much later start is rapidly catching up to competitor/customer Anthropic. SpaceX data centers will also be in high demand from Tesla's FSD cars and Optimus robots.  Anthropic is the leader in coding digital ai.  We believe Grok will be the leader in physical ai due to its engineering expertise in materials, cars, rockets, robots and material science.

One more thing.  I am in Palm Beach today and just picked up my new Premium Model Y L.  The office manager told me he has 48 cars scheduled for delivery today.  Yesterday he delivered 36.  Last year the day before Thanksgiving he delivered 4!  Told me everyone is buying the car for FSD!!!!  Just sayin...

--

full_text_zh:
“观看埃隆工程师就像观看迈克尔·乔丹打篮球......”- SpaceX 总监。 2026 年 10 月

这是对我的问题“Elon 真的是一位令人难以置信的工程师吗？”的回答。 一位 SpaceX 董事最近与我交谈时说道。 因此，@elonmusk 不仅是一位超级工程师……物理学家……和未来的想象家……他还是一位准备充分的企业家。 这意味着他可以利用像现在这样的金融市场混乱。 这对@SpaceX 和@Tesla 来说是巨大的好处。

其他人建造的数据中心每千兆瓦的平均成本为 600 亿美元……平均需要 30 个月才能投入使用……而当它们投入使用时，往往会遇到初始运营问题。 所谓的 Neocloud 提供商每年以约 120 亿美元的价格建造和租赁此类项目。 对他们来说不幸的是，虽然对数据中心支持的超级智能的需求呈指数级增长，但此类项目目前很难获得债务融资。 先进的芯片也是如此。

另一方面，SpaceX 拥有堡垒式的资产负债表……能够完成此类复杂的工程项目，并在不到八个月的时间内启动它们……我们估计价值 350 亿美元……并根据可再生租赁将其出租给超大规模企业及其最大客户@Anthropic，为期六个月或更长时间，每年费用超过 500 亿美元！ 这是由于巨大的 SI 需求似乎呈指数级增长。 佐维！ 意味着他们在八个月内赚回了全部数据中心投资！

哦，是的。 差点忘了。 与资产负债表脆弱的 Neocloud 不同，SpaceX 是一家垂直开发商，目前它们作为合同建造者很难获得融资。 除了目前其他公司对其数据中心的强劲需求外，目前正在建设并出租给其他公司的数据中心很快将被其Grok超级智能部门使用。 Grok 起步较晚，但正在迅速赶上竞争对手/客户 Anthropic。特斯拉的 FSD 汽车和 Optimus 机器人也对 SpaceX 数据中心有很高的需求。 Anthropic 是数字人工智能编码领域的领导者。 我们相信，由于 Grok 在材料、汽车、火箭、机器人和材料科学方面的工程专业知识，Grok 将成为物理人工智能领域的领导者。

还有一件事。 我今天在棕榈滩，刚刚收到了我的新高级 Model Y L。办公室经理告诉我，他今天计划交付 48 辆汽车。 昨天他交付了 36 个。去年感恩节前一天他交付了 4 个！ 告诉我大家买车都是为了FSD！ 就说...

title: First of its kind: TheSystem - I released TheSystem, a model that decides when to decide and when to generate text. TheSystem is open.
title_en: First of its kind: TheSystem - I released TheSystem, a model that decides when to decide and when to generate text. TheSystem is open.
title_zh: 模型控制架构TheSystem开源发布
author: @LeszBuk
summary_en: Independent developer Lesz Buk has released TheSystem, an open-source model designed to dynamically control the timing of text generation through a dedicated decision engine. The architecture introduces a logic layer that autonomously determines when the model should deliberate versus when it should initiate text output.
summary_zh: 独立开发者Lesz Buk发布开源模型TheSystem，引入基于决策判断的动态生成控制架构。
full_text_zh: 第一个：TheSystem - 我发布了 TheSystem，一个决定何时做出决定以及何时生成文本的模型。系统已开放。
full_text_en: First of its kind: TheSystem - I released TheSystem, a model that decides when to decide and when to generate text. TheSystem is open.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 独立开发者Lesz Buk正式发布开源模型TheSystem，该模型旨在通过决策引擎动态控制文本生成的时机。此系统核心在于在推理过程中增加了一层判断逻辑，从而在“决定执行任务”与“执行生成任务”之间实现自主分流。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Independent developer Lesz Buk has released TheSystem, an open-source model designed to dynamically control the timing of text generation through a dedicated decision engine. The architecture introduces a logic layer that autonomously determines when the model should deliberate versus when it should initiate text output.

elements_zh.where: 开源技术社区
elements_zh.what: 发布具备自主决策与文本生成控制能力的TheSystem模型
elements_zh.why: 优化大模型推理过程中的决策效率与生成逻辑

elements_en.what: Released TheSystem with autonomous decision-making and generation control
elements_en.why: To optimize efficiency and logical sequencing in model inference

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该架构通过将‘决策权’从提示词工程（Prompt Engineering）下沉至模型内部逻辑，是迈向系统级推理（System 2 Thinking）的重要技术探索。其价值在于大幅降低了对于预定义思维链的依赖，为边缘侧小参数模型实现复杂的任务规划提供了新的架构思路。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This architecture shifts decision-making from prompt engineering to internal logic, representing a critical step toward System 2 reasoning. Its core value lies in reducing reliance on predefined CoT prompts and providing a scalable blueprint for edge-side models to handle complex task planning.

The architecture introduces a logic layer that autonomously determines when the model should deliberate versus when it should initiate text output.

实现从强制推理向动态自适应推理的架构转型
通过开源模式推进推理成本优化与任务规划研究

Transitioning from forced CoT to dynamic, adaptive inference
Advancing inference cost reduction via open-source development

title: A successful test-time compute paradigm has always been a north star of AI because if we can actually arbitrarily improve model capability as a function of how much test-time compute we put in, in principle you would be able to put in 1B, 10B, or even 1T token
title_en:
A successful test-time compute paradigm has always been a north star of AI because if we can actually arbitrarily improve model capability as a function of how much test-time compute we put in, in principle you would be able to put in 1B, 10B, or even 1T tokens into a really hard problem and be assured that you would make progress

While we always talk about how to improve pretraining scaling law coefficients, i feel that we talk less about the slope of scaling laws in test-time compute, which matters a lot if you truly have conviction that we will one day spend trillions of tokens trying to solve the hardest problems

It turns out that one of the benchmarks that @jake_cole1 built recently is a great tool for measuring this slope of test-time compute scaling: models spend O(100M) tokens doing the tasks on average, with no signs of saturation on the test time compute curve. The benchmark comprises long-horizon engineering tasks ranging from optimizing kernels to designing an aircraft.

An interesting finding is that the open source models don't have as good of a test-time compute curve as our favorite frontier models. Obviously scale as a factor here, as Astra outperforms Sol and Fable outperforms Opus. In some sense this is good measure of model size too, as larger models obviously be more performant per token. You can change the x-axis to cost too and things shift around, though that's also somewhat over-tethered to the current pricing of the models

Another cool thing that this benchmark provides is it has both provided test cases and hidden test cases, to test the generality of solutions given by AI when such generality is expected. Argon has the biggest gap by far (35%) of the models evaluated, which means it provides solutions that meet specified criteria but may not be very general

Read more in our arxiv paper that just came out: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.30017
title_zh:
成功的测试时计算范式一直是人工智能的北极星，因为如果我们实际上可以根据我们投入的测试时计算量来随意提高模型能力，原则上你将能够将 1B、10B 甚至 1T 代币放入一个真正困难的问题中，并确保你会取得进展

虽然我们总是谈论如何改进预训练标
author: Jason Wei
author_role: OpenAI 核心研究员 / 思维链 (CoT) 与涌现能力提出者
summary_zh:
度律系数，但我觉得我们很少谈论测试时计算中标度律的斜率，如果你真的相信我们有一天会花费数万亿代币来尝试解决最困难的问题，那么这一点就很重要

事实证明，@jake_cole1 最近构建的基准测试之一是测量测试时间计算扩展斜率的一个很好的工具：模型平均花费 O(100M) 个令牌来执行任务，测试时间计算曲线上没有饱和的迹象。该基准包括长期工程任务，从优化内核到设计飞机。

一个有趣的发现是，开源模型的测试时间计算曲线不如我们最喜欢的前沿模型。显然，规模是这里的一个因素，因为《Astra》优于《Sol》，《Fable》优于《Opus》。从某种意义上说，这也是衡量模型大小的好方法，因为较大的模型显然每个令牌的性能都更高。您也可以将 x 轴更改为成本，并且情况会发生变化，尽管这也有点过度依赖于模型的当前定价

该基准测试提供的另一件很酷的事情是，它同时提供了测试用例和隐藏测试用例，以在预期人工智能给出的解决方案具有通用性时测试这种通用性。迄今为止，Argon 在评估的模型中差距最大 (35%)，这意味着它提供的解决方案满足指定标准，但可能不是很通用

请阅读我们刚刚发表的 arxiv 论文了解更多内容：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.30017

Our agent reverse engineers software, rewires it for its own use, and builds an MCP server to interact with it.

title: Feedback is a gift. And this is one thing agents are definitely better at giving it than humans. A person tells you about the last thing that annoyed them. An agent doesn't have same recency bias. It reads the whole repo, including the workarounds you forgot you
title_en:
Feedback is a gift. And this is one thing agents are definitely better at giving it than humans.

A person tells you about the last thing that annoyed them. An agent doesn't have same recency bias. It reads the whole repo, including the workarounds you forgot you wrote.

We added feedback to the Cloudflare MCP and the cf CLI. Or paste this prompt into any repo with a Cloudflare project. Your agent writes up the friction and sends it to us.

The full loop is eventually fixes near realtime with MCP events letting you know its done.

http://gist.github.com/dknecht/6fe895c765724ac034dfc84a8f53d3b7

Feedback is a gift. And this is one thing agents are definitely better at giving it than humans.

title: Your AI agent's instructions, permissions, and data rules deserve the same care as your code. Review them together in one place, then approve and ship. 🚢 But approval on paper isn't enough. The rules have to be enforced every time the agent takes an action

Your AI agent's instructions, permissions, and data rules deserve the same care as your code.

Review them together in one place, then approve and ship. 🚢

But approval on paper isn't enough. The rules have to be enforced every time the agent takes an action. 

Redpanda's Ben Barkhouse shows how to manage AI agents like code with the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane. 👉 http://bit.ly/4AZbQ2p

但纸上的批准还不够。每次代理采取行动时都必须执行这些规则。

title: AgentX is the first industry-standard LLM inference benchmark to feature Trainium, TPU, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and OpenAI's custom Jalapeño ASIC (and soon Huawei and Alibaba's PPU). AgentX is supported by almost every major buyer of compute, from
title_en:
AgentX is the first industry-standard LLM inference benchmark to feature Trainium, TPU, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and OpenAI's custom Jalapeño ASIC (and soon Huawei and Alibaba's PPU).

AgentX is supported by almost every major buyer of compute, from Microsoft Azure to Amazon, Google, Oracle, Meta, and many more. Furthermore, it has the support of the ML community, including vLLM, LMCache, SGLang, PyTorch, and Hugging Face, as well as major AI labs like OpenAI, MiniMax, ZAI, Qwen, Moonshot Kimi, etc. (4/5)

title: No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For
title_en:
No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different. For example in an interview on CBS a couple months ago, I specifically called for AI to be governed democratically. I call for the same in Policy on the AI Exponential, Machines of Loving Grace, and The Adolescence of Technology, and We Must Pace the Frontier. Machines of Loving Grace contains an extended section on using AI to revitalize democracy, and discusses the use of AI as an aid to citizens in their decision-making, "aggregat[ing] opinions and driv[ing] consensus among citizens, resolving conflict, finding common ground, and seeking compromise.” The clear and obvious implication is that humans should remain the ones making political and governance decisions. The Adolescence of Technology has an entire section on fighting against AI-driven tyranny, and I even discuss the danger of AI labs usurping power and come out strongly against it — by implication, this definitely includes an AI lab usurping power and giving it to AI itself!

If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years. But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.

Separately, I think there is frequent conflation (including in this article) between the idea of “surrendering human free will” to AI in some grand sense of global governance, and the more prosaic idea that as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way. This is not AI “running the world,” but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end. Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc. It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives. But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.

For example, using AI too autonomously to build the next generation of AI systems (known as recursive self-improvement, or RSI) may cause AI to improve faster than we can control or adjust to it, so we may want limits on this process. As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding. Second, in some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption, and it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt. Third, while the use of AI for alignment research is an incredibly valuable tool, it must be done with caution, because we may not be able to trust the work of the AI system. Finally, in many cases, humans would simply prefer to do some activities themselves, so they can stay deeply engaged in what matters to them, even if AI can do those activities better. There are countless other examples and hard cases. I don’t think there are any easy answers here, nor is there (nor should there be) any single decision-maker: some of these decisions will be made by society, some by government, some by AI companies, and some in a decentralized manner by individuals expressing their own preferences as consumers, which may differ from the preferences of others.

I don't think that other AI leaders or AI companies have significantly different views from me on whether specific tasks should be automated. Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation (as that’s been the general consequence of scaling up AI training), and every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards. If anything, Anthropic has been the most vocal and the most proactive about acknowledging these downsides and trying to address them. For instance, it’s fairly absurd to cite my statement that fully autonomous weapons might “one day be needed for the defense of democracy” as differing from that of other AI companies, when I was willing to risk Anthropic’s future as a company to refuse to allow our existing AI models to be used for autonomous weapons even in the face of legal sanctions, and no other AI company did the same.

To summarize, as applied to grand questions of how we govern increasingly capable AI, I have been vocal and consistent that AI needs to be governed by a legitimate, democratic process and that “surrendering human free will” to AI systems is a terrible idea. As applied to automation of specific tasks by or for people, my views are more mixed, but I don’t think they differ from those of other AI companies — most other companies seem to be offering similar products and confronting similar tradeoffs without having perfect answers to them. What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like “human control and agency,” or “AI should be just a tool,” without actually doing anything different in their products or taking seriously the difficult questions that lie behind these slogans.
title_zh: 不，我不认为我们应该向人工智能系统“投降人类自由意志”，而且建议我这样做是荒谬的。我写了数百页的文章，其中一个不变的主题是人工智能需要受到合法的民主程序的治理。几千年来（一直追溯到希腊和罗马哲学家），独裁制的拥护者声称，与混乱的民主过程相比
author: @DarioAmodei
summary_zh:
独裁制可以带来更好、更快或更果断的决策。即使这是真的（我对此表示怀疑！），我们也不应该为了效率或安全而牺牲合法性或自决权。这种反对专制的论点逐字逐句地适用于反对人工智能治理，我同样强烈地认为，将治理交给人工智能是一个坏主意。

没有人仔细阅读过我的文章或我的采访，可以合理地得出我相信任何不同的东西的结论。例如，在几个月前接受哥伦比亚广播公司采访时，我特别呼吁对人工智能进行民主治理。我在《人工智能指数政策》、《慈爱机器》、《技术青春期》和《我们必须走在前沿》中呼吁同样的做法。 《爱的机器》包含了关于使用人工智能重振民主的扩展部分，并讨论了使用人工智能作为公民决策的辅助手段，“聚集公民意见并推动公民共识，解决冲突，寻找共同点，寻求妥协。”明确而明显的含义是，人类应该仍然是政治和治理决策的制定者。 《科技青春期》有一整节都是在反对人工智能驱动的暴政，我什至讨论了人工智能实验室篡夺权力的危险，并强烈反对它——暗示，这肯定包括人工智能实验室篡夺权力并将其交给人工智能本身！

如果我认为这是一个好主意，我就会在公开场合倡导它，就像过去几年我并不害怕倡导许多不受欢迎的观点一样。但我并不提倡这样做，因为我认为将治理交给人工智能是一个糟糕的主意。

另外，我认为在某种宏观意义上的全球治理中“让人类自由意志屈服于人工智能”的想法与随着人工智能系统的进步，它们变得能够以更自动化的方式完成特定任务的更平淡的想法之间经常存在混淆（包括在本文中）。这不是人工智能“统治世界”，而是人工智能驾驶汽车、设计抗癌药物或端到端编写软件。在这里，我的观点是复杂的。人工智能完成更完整或更大规模的任务具有经济价值，可以推动软件、医学、交通、能源等领域的重要进步。在许多情况下，这显然是可取的，并且将挽救大量生命。但它也有缺点，在某些领域可能不值得。

例如，过于自主地使用人工智能来构建下一代人工智能系统（称为递归自我改进，或RSI）可能会导致人工智能的改进速度超过我们控制或调整的速度，因此我们可能希望限制这一过程。正如我们在 11 月初公开表示的那样，我们认为克劳德在没有有意义的人类监督或理解的情况下完全自主地构建连续的前沿模型是不安全的。其次，在某些情况下，以过于端到端的方式使用人工智能可能会导致严重的工作中断，因此放慢甚至停止某些人工智能部署以使人们有更多时间适应可能是有意义的。第三，虽然使用人工智能进行比对研究是一种非常有价值的工具，但必须谨慎行事，因为我们可能无法信任人工智能系统的工作。最后，在许多情况下，人类只是更喜欢自己做一些活动，这样他们就可以深入参与对他们来说重要的事情，即使人工智能可以更好地完成这些活动。还有无数其他例子和疑难案例。我认为这里没有任何简单的答案，也不存在（也不应该有）任何单一的决策者：其中一些决策将由社会做出，一些由政府做出，一些由人工智能公司做出，还有一些以去中心化的方式由个人作为消费者表达自己的偏好，这些偏好可能与其他人的偏好不同。

我认为其他人工智能领导者或人工智能公司对于特定任务是否应该自动化的看法与我没有显着不同。当然，他们提供的产品在任务自动化方面没有重大差异；每家公司似乎都在发布越来越能够实现任务自动化的模型（因为这是扩大人工智能培训的普遍结果），并且每家公司都声称了解这种自动化的风险和缺点，并提供保障措施。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是 Anthropic 是最直言不讳、最积极主动地承认这些缺点并试图解决它们的。例如，引用我的陈述，即“有一天可能需要完全自主武器来捍卫民主”，与其他人工智能公司的说法不同，这是相当荒谬的，因为我愿意冒着 Anthropic 公司未来的风险，拒绝允许我们现有的人工智能模型用于自主武器，即使面临法律制裁，而且没有其他人工智能公司这样做。

总而言之，当应用于我们如何治理能力日益强大的人工智能这一重大问题时，我一直直言不讳地表示，人工智能需要由合法、民主的程序来治理，而向人工智能系统“投降人类自由意志”是一个糟糕的想法。当应用于由人或为人执行特定任务的自动化时，我的观点更加复杂，但我认为它们与其他人工智能公司的观点没有什么不同——大多数其他公司似乎都提供类似的产品并面临类似的权衡，但没有完美的答案。正在发生的事情是，一些人工智能首席执行官正在从事一种基于氛围的商业和政治定位，他们重复诸如“人类控制和代理”或“人工智能应该只是一种工具”之类的口号，而没有在他们的产品中实际做任何不同的事情，也没有认真对待这些口号背后的难题。

title: As a physicist, people often ask me if I have an opinion on when quantum computers will be scaled enough to pose a threat to RSA public key cryptography through Shor’s algorithm. I’m not too worried about that right now. In my opinion, the immediate risk is a
title_en:
As a physicist, people often ask me if I have an opinion on when quantum computers will be scaled enough to pose a threat to RSA public key cryptography through Shor’s algorithm. I’m not too worried about that right now.

In my opinion, the immediate risk is a math discovery through LLMs that allows factoring in polynomial time on a classical computer. We haven’t been able to prove that this is impossible, and factoring is in a special place where a polynomial algorithm would not imply P=NP.

On the other hand, if an LLM proves that factoring isn’t possible in polynomial time on a classical computer, that would be great!
